routes.label: Encode repdigits and verify the complete decimal identity

changes.rationale: For n repeated digits, write T=10^n, a=8(T-1)/9 and b=5(T-1)/9. Then 9ab=40(T-1)^2/9. Its decimal expansion has n-1 fours, then 3, then n-1 fives, then 60; the geometric sums verify the entire expansion, including n=1. The digit sum is 9n=17865, C. Reuse the revised C repdigit-product-digits proposal. Node 024 concerns changing numeral bases and does not cover this long-decimal carry analysis.

answerCheck.reason: With k repeated digits, a=8(10^k-1)/9 and b=5(10^k-1)/9, so 9ab=40(10^k-1)^2/9. A verified decimal expansion is k-1 copies of 4, then 3, then k-1 copies of 5, then 60. In powers of ten it is 4*sum(10^j,j=k+2..2k)+3*10^(k+1)+5*sum(10^j,j=2..k)+60; the two geometric sums give exactly the preceding product. Its digit sum is 4(k-1)+3+5(k-1)+6=9k=17865. Empty sums make the formula valid at k=1 too.
